root.label: Fundamental types
root.note: Minimum widths and an ordering, then promotion and the usual arithmetic conversions before every operator.

children.label: Integer guarantees
children.note: The standard fixes minimum widths and a range ordering, not exact sizes.

children.label: Minimum widths
children.note: signed char, short, int, long, long long: at least 8, 16, 16, 32 and 64 bits.

children.label: LP64 vs LLP64
children.note: long is 64 bits on Linux and macOS but 32 bits on 64-bit Windows.

children.label: Two's complement (C++20)
children.note: Signed range is exactly -2^(N-1) to 2^(N-1)-1; integer conversions wrap modulo 2^N.

children.label: Overflow still UB
children.note: Signed arithmetic that leaves the type's range is undefined even in C++20.

children.label: char
children.note: char, signed char and unsigned char are three distinct types.

children.label: Signedness
children.note: Implementation-defined: signed on x86-64 Linux and Apple arm64, unsigned on arm64 Linux.

children.label: Character types
children.note: char8_t, char16_t, char32_t and wchar_t are distinct types with underlying integer types.

children.label: Integral promotion
children.note: Operands narrower than int are widened before arithmetic.

children.label: Small to int
children.note: char, short and their variants become int if int holds all values, else unsigned int.

children.label: bool to int
children.note: false becomes 0 and true becomes 1, so true + true is the int 2.

children.label: Wide characters
children.note: Promote to the first of int, unsigned, long and so on that fits; char32_t usually becomes unsigned.

children.label: unsigned short trap
children.note: Two large unsigned shorts multiply as signed int and can overflow: undefined behavior.

children.label: Usual conversions
children.note: [expr.arith.conv] brings both operands of a binary operator to one common type.

children.label: Conversion rank
children.note: long long > long > int > short > signed char; unsigned matches signed; bool is lowest.

children.label: Floating wins
children.note: An integer operand converts to the floating type; between floats, the lower rank converts.

children.label: Unsigned wins ties
children.note: If the unsigned type's rank is at least the signed one's, the signed operand becomes unsigned.

children.label: Platform-dependent case
children.note: A wider signed type absorbs the unsigned one only if it can represent all of its values.

children.label: Enum mixing
children.note: Enum with float, or two enum types, was deprecated in C++20 and is ill-formed in C++26.

children.label: Comparison traps
children.note: Mixed-sign comparisons convert negatives into huge unsigned values.

children.label: -1 < 0u is false
children.note: Same rank, so -1 converts to UINT_MAX before comparing.

children.label: size() - 1
children.note: On an empty container the subtraction wraps to the maximum size_t value.

children.label: std::cmp_less (C++20)
children.note: Compares the mathematical values of any two standard integer types.

children.label: Other types
children.note: bool, fixed-width integers and the floating types.

children.label: bool conversion
children.note: Zero, null pointer and null member pointer become false; everything else true.

children.label: Fixed-width integers
children.note: std::intN_t is optional; std::int_leastN_t and std::int_fastN_t always exist.

children.label: Extended floats (C++23)
children.note: std::float16_t and friends in <stdfloat>; implicit conversion to a lower rank is not allowed.
